questions.stem: What three conditions are needed for a seed to germinate?

options.text: Water, oxygen, and a suitable temperature
Carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight
Light, soil, and fertiliser
Minerals, warmth, and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Seeds need water (to activate enzymes and swell the seed), oxygen (for aerobic respiration to provide energy), and a suitable temperature (for enzyme activity). Light is not needed for germination itself, as the seed has its own food store.

questions.stem: Why does a seed need water for germination?

options.text: To dissolve minerals from the soil
To carry out photosynthesis
To produce chlorophyll
To activate enzymes and soften the seed coat

questions.explanation: Water is absorbed by the seed, causing it to swell and soften the seed coat (testa). Water also activates enzymes that break down the food stores (such as starch to glucose) to provide energy for growth.

questions.stem: What is the food store used by the germinating seed before it can photosynthesise?

options.text: Glucose produced by the seed coat
Minerals absorbed from the soil
Starch stored in the cotyledons or endosperm
Proteins absorbed from water

questions.explanation: Seeds contain food stores (mainly starch) in the cotyledons (seed leaves) or endosperm. During germination, enzymes break down starch into glucose, which is used in respiration to provide energy for growth until the seedling can photosynthesise.

questions.stem: Which part of the seed emerges first during germination?

options.text: The shoot (plumule)
The root (radicle)
The flower
The leaves

questions.explanation: The root (radicle) emerges first from the germinating seed. This anchors the seedling in the soil and begins absorbing water and minerals. The shoot (plumule) then grows upwards towards the light.

questions.stem: Why does a germinating seed need oxygen?

options.text: To dissolve the seed coat
To produce chlorophyll
For photosynthesis
For aerobic respiration to release energy for growth

questions.explanation: The germinating seed needs oxygen for aerobic respiration. Respiration breaks down the stored glucose to release energy (ATP) needed for cell division and growth. Without oxygen, germination is very slow or cannot occur.

questions.stem: What is the role of the enzyme amylase during germination?

options.text: It breaks down starch into maltose (sugar)
It breaks down the seed coat
It breaks down proteins into amino acids
It converts glucose into starch for storage

questions.explanation: Amylase is an enzyme that breaks down starch (the main food store in many seeds) into maltose, which is further broken down into glucose. This glucose is then used in respiration to provide energy for the growing seedling.

questions.stem: Why is a suitable temperature important for germination?

options.text: Because photosynthesis only works at high temperatures
Because the seed coat only dissolves at high temperatures
Because enzymes involved in germination work best within a specific temperature range
Because seeds need to be at exactly 100 degrees C

questions.explanation: The enzymes that break down food stores and drive growth during germination have an optimum temperature range. If it is too cold, enzyme activity is too slow; if too hot, enzymes denature. This is why different species germinate best at different temperatures.
